name: Huppah
overview: Huppah was a male Levite who served as the thirteenth chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the sons of Aaron, which positioned him within a significant priestly lineage. His role as one of the appointed priests highlights his part in the organized worship and service of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Huppah means 'canopy, hence protection,' reflecting a possible symbolic association with shelter or covering. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:13 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Huppah as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a prominent priestly family within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Huppah's significance lies in his appointment as one of the twenty-four priestly courses, specifically as the thirteenth chosen from the line of Eleazar. This organization of priests was crucial for the orderly functioning of temple duties and worship in Israel. His inclusion in this system reflects the fulfillment of God's provision for structured priestly service through the descendants of Aaron.
